newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian Authority says sharp 1996 drop in GDP.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian Authority says sharp 1996 drop in GDP.

text.p: The Palestinian Monetary Authority (PMA) said on Tuesday that real Palestinian gross domestic product fell to $1.633 billion in 1996 from $2.161 billion in 1995 due to Israeli closures of the West Bank and Gaza.

In a statement on 1996 economic activity, the PMA, which acts as a central bank but does not issue currency, estimated that the Palestinian economy lost $1.2 billion over 118 days of full closures that prevented workers from reaching jobs in Israel and curtailed trade.
Israel imposed a blanket closure on the West Bank and Gaza Strip in February 1996 following the first of four suicide bombings by Islamic militants that killed 59 in Israel.
The closure, which was gradually eased, was imposed again in September after fresh clashes between Israeli and PLO security forces claimed the lives of 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.
The PMA statement said annual per capita income in the West Bank and Gaza Strip was $652, slightly higher than the officially defined poverty line of $650.
The statement put average unemployment in 1996 at 60 percent in the Gaza Strip and 38 percent in the West Bank.
"These developments have aggravated poverty in Palestinian society. Sixty-five percent of Palestinian families are now below the poverty line," the statement said.
The PMA said the Palestinian Authority's budget deficit rose to $195 million in 1996 from $75 million in 1995.
Inflation in the West Bank and Gaza Strip reached 12 percent in 1996 compared with 11 percent in Israel, the statement said.

The statement also said that donor countries that had pledged $2.4 billion after the landmark 1993 Israeli-PLO self-rule deal had so far delivered a total of $985 million, far below the losses incurred by the Palestinian economy in 1996 due to Israeli closures.
